description:
fz removed `&&`, `||` and `!` (0f9f0a057, fz-b7n) as C-style duplicates of `and`/`or`/`not`. In Elixir they are different operators, and fz follows Elixir for operators:

- `and`/`or`/`not` are strict: the left operand (the operand, for `not`) must be a boolean.
- `&&`, `||` and `!` take any value. `nil` and `false` count as false, everything else as true, and the result is the deciding value: `nil || []` is `[]`, `"x" || []` is `"x"`, `nil && 1` is `nil`, `!nil` is `true`. They are Kernel macros in Elixir and are not allowed in guards.

The distiller uses `||` for a default when a key is missing (tools/distill-telemetry.exs:155-156), and today stops there: "`||` is not an operator; use `or`".

Acceptance: all three parse at Elixir precedence and give Elixir's results on interp, run and build, checked against an Elixir oracle (truthiness table, returned values, short-circuit: the right side is not evaluated when the left decides, precedence against `and`/`or`/`|>`/comparisons); a guard using one is refused with a clear error, as Elixir refuses it. The "use `or`" lexer message is removed. Proposal page before building.
title: &&, || and ! with Elixir's meaning
